name: in-the-air-tonight
description: FAMOUS DRUM SOUND #4: Phil Collins 'In the Air Tonight' (Hugh Padgham, 1981) — the GATED-REVERB sound that defined the 1980s. A NEW axis vs the room-warm Bonham 'fool-in-the-rain', the mono-crush Beatles 'tomorrow-never-knows' and the clean-dynamic 'home-at-last': EXPLOSIVE / GATED / HUGE — a big, slightly dark room ambience that is HEAVILY COMPRESSED and then cut off ABRUPTLY by a noise gate (no decaying tail), blended big under the dry kit and spread WIDE. Built deterministically in PURE DSP: a seeded decaying-noise reverb IR -> compress-loop crush -> an abrupt envelope gate keyed off the dry kit (derived from scripts/mix/keyed_gate.py) -> wide blend. Does NOT need room mics (the bus SYNTHESIZES the room — the inverse of fool-in-the-rain). This is the gated-reverb TONE, not a groove. Dev-validated 2026-06-04 on a 60 s watercolors drum bus; the default path is BIT-REPRODUCIBLE (no VST, no UADx). Honest era PROXY of the SSL-channel comp+gate -> AMS/Lexicon ambience technique (see notes).
pipeline: 1. SOURCE: phase-aligned multi-mic stems (kick + snare + toms + hi-hat + overheads). NO room mics required — the bus generates its own gated ambience (the OPPOSITE of fool-in-the-rain). A snare/tom-forward kit suits the iconic gated-fill sound.

2. PER-STEM PROCESS: scripts/mix/process_stems.py with presets/mix/in-the-air-tonight-stem-process.plans.json (PUNCHY + DRY + tight: controlled lows, present snare/tom CRACK, transient snap ALLOWED here so the dry hits cut through the explosion and key the gate cleanly; declick OFF) -> <kit>/processed-iat/.
3. SNARE/TOM-FORWARD balance: scripts/mix/balance_stems.py with the per-role targets below (measured LUFS) -> bus_iat_pre.wav.

4. IN-THE-AIR-TONIGHT BUS: scripts/mix/in_the_air_tonight_bus.py bus_iat_pre.wav bus_iat.wav (synth reverb -> heavy compression -> abrupt gate -> wet/dry blend -> present EQ -> WIDE; params in that script).

balance_targets_lufs._method: measured integrated LUFS per stem, gained to target; one global -6 dBFS-peak headroom trim on the sum (NOT peak-normalized per stem). SNARE/TOM-FORWARD: the gated snare + tom fills are the 80s stars, kick solid, overheads/hat present but under the drums (the gated explosion is added at the BUS, not from a room mic).

snare top._note: THE STAR — the gated snare; full body + crack, keyed into the bus gate

tom._note: the iconic tom FILL (if present) — forward; pan spread across multiple tom mics

kick in._note: solid, punchy, controlled — drives the groove under the explosion

overhead._note: kit image (stereo) — present but the bus owns the 'room'

snare bottom._note: a touch of wires/snap under the top

hi hat._note: present but restrained (the iconic intro had none — keep it modest)

drum room._note: OPTIONAL + FAR DOWN — the BUS makes the gated room; a real room channel is redundant here (omit it)

bus_chain._impl: scripts/mix/in_the_air_tonight_bus.py — authoritative; a bare invocation reproduces these BIT-FOR-BIT (deterministic: seeded synth reverb + compress-loop + numpy gate; no VST loaded on the default path).
1_eq_pre_zero_phase: high_pass 30 Hz q0.707 (subsonic; keep rumble out of the reverb)

2_synth_reverb._intent: a big, slightly dark room ambience generated from the dry kit. White noise * exp-decay, LPF dark + HPF 120, energy-normalized; two seeds (L/R) = a WIDE decorrelated room. Deterministic (seeded). --reverb-vst routes a real reverb instead, but that path is NOT the locked signature (load != render).

3_heavy_compression._intent: CRUSH the ambience so it EXPLODES — the SSL talkback-comp move. Auto-makeup (RMS-match) brings the crushed room back up to a big level. This is the engine of the gated-reverb 'whoomph'.

4_abrupt_gate.impl: envelope gate keyed off the DRY kit
4_abrupt_gate._intent: the SIGNATURE: opens instantly on a hit, HOLDS open ~320 ms, then SLAMS shut (28 ms release) = the reverb has NO decaying tail. Keyed off the dry kit env (5 ms smoothing, 80th-pctile * thresh_pct) so it opens exactly on hits. Derived from scripts/mix/keyed_gate.py. Do NOT soften the close — the abrupt cutoff IS the sound.

5_blend._intent: the gated explosion sits UNDER the dry hits, RMS-matched to the dry first so --wet is a meaningful ratio. 0.7 = a big but not drowning blend.

6_eq_post_zero_phase: bell 4000 +2.0 dB q1.0 (the explosive snare CRACK)

7_stereo_width._intent: WIDE — the HUGE 80s image (the OPPOSITE of tomorrow-never-knows' mono). The synth IR is already decorrelated L/R; width 1.4 spreads the explosion across the field.

bus_chain.8_output: peak-normalize to -1 dBFS (mix bus — NOT mastered)

approved_signature_full_kit._measured_on: a 60 s watercolors drum bus (bus_punchy_pre.wav): pre-bus centroid 2223 / tilt -2.22 / crest 21.6 / corr 0.981 / LUFS -25.8. PLACEHOLDER pending the .claude/workflows/in-the-air-tonight.js Gemini judge panel; the default render is BIT-REPRODUCIBLE (md5-identical across re-renders — no VST/UADx on the default path), so once the panel picks a winner, a sequential re-render reproduces it exactly.
approved_signature_full_kit._what_to_check: the DIRECTION, not absolutes: (1) correlation DROPS HARD (0.981->0.494) = WIDE/HUGE — the defining 80s spread (the inverse of TNK's ~0.99 mono). (2) LUFS jumps UP (-25.8->-18.7) at the SAME -1 dBFS peak = the dense, exploding ambience filling the gaps. (3) centroid UP (2223->2912) = the present snare CRACK. (4) crest stays HIGH (21.6->21.0) = the dry transients punch THROUGH the explosion (the gate truncates the tail rather than smearing the hits). The gated-vs-ungated difference is mostly PERCEPTUAL (the abrupt tail cutoff), not in these 5 integrated meters — judge the tail by ear/the Gemini panel.

notes: This is the gated-reverb TONE — a heavily-compressed room cut off abruptly by a gate, blended big and wide. It is the 1980s drum-production signature, not a specific groove.

Does NOT need room mics — the bus SYNTHESIZES the gated ambience from the dry kit (the OPPOSITE of fool-in-the-rain, which needs a real room channel). A real room mic is redundant here; omit it or keep it far down.

EXPLOSIVE = the heavy compression of the ambience (the SSL talkback-comp move); GATED = the abrupt close (no decaying tail); HUGE = the wide blend. All three are the point — do not soften any of them.

DETERMINISTIC default: the synth reverb (seeded RNG) + compress-loop + numpy gate are pure DSP — a bare invocation is bit-reproducible (no VST, no UADx non-determinism). This is the only famous-drum recipe whose default path loads no plugin.

Optional --reverb-vst <path> routes a real reverb (e.g. ValhallaPlate / SSL Native FlexVerb) instead of the synth IR — a CREATIVE alternative, NOT the locked signature. load != render: verify the VST actually processed (a 0.00 change = passthrough) before trusting it ([[vst-reverb]] / [[vst-verify]]).

HONEST NUANCE (the real recording): the gated-reverb sound was DISCOVERED by engineer Hugh Padgham on Peter Gabriel's 'Intruder' (1980) at Townhouse Studios when an SSL 4000 talkback/overhead mic — with the console channel's compressor + noise gate engaged — was left open over the kit; it was then used on Phil Collins' 'In the Air Tonight' (1981). The era effect = a heavily-compressed ambient mic into a noise gate (and later AMS RMX16 'NonLin' / Lexicon ambience). This chain is an era-appropriate PROXY of that technique in deterministic DSP, NOT a model of the literal Townhouse signal path.
This is a MIX bus (peak -1, NOT mastered) — hand to master-track for loudness/limiting and loops-to-deliverables for loops.
